notes: §2002:14.8.25.2 SR3 asks a MULTIPLY literal to be a numeric literal, and a floating-point literal is one only as §2002:8.3.1.2.2.2 forms it: a significand of 1 through 31 digits and an exponent of at most three (rules 2-3). NumericLiteral.CheckFloatingPointForm takes the edition's limits (DialectBehavior.FloatingLiteralWideLimits, from 2014 36 and four), so at --std 2002 MULTIPLY 1.00000000000000000000000000000000E0 BY W-N (a 33-digit significand) is refused, COBOL1661 (kb/Work PB5613).
